_doc: Curated technique seeds (knowledge_architecture.md section 5), one file per area. Fields: id, level + scope (a scope node or universal), aliases (v1 / technique-DB / footer names folded in), mechanism, preconditions (predicate DSL), predicts (canonical metric -> up|down|flat|up_or_flat|down_or_flat), risks (pitfalls), states / op_classes / op_kinds gates (empty = any), slot (offered by the multi-slot agent), prior {mean, n}: a seed prior with a low pseudo-count that evidence overrides, realizations by scope (target:<key> | target:<backend>:sm_NN+ | target:<backend> | node:<id> | universal). Loaded by Ontology.seed(); scripts/seed_knowledge.py builds a knowledge.db from these files.

techniques.mechanism: reduce in registers across the lanes of a warp / subgroup, with no shared-memory round trips or barriers per step

realizations.how: Reduce within a warp with __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, v, o) for o = 16..1, then across warps via a 32-entry shared array and one more warp reduction.
sub_group_reduce_add / sub_group_reduce_max (cl_khr_subgroups; on Adreno a subgroup is a half or full 64-wide wave), then across subgroups via __local.

techniques.mechanism: map one block (or warp) to each reduced row and parallelise the reduced dimension, so every lane has work

realizations.how: Map one block (or one warp / subgroup for short rows) to each reduced row; threads stride over the row with coalesced loads, then a block reduction.

techniques.mechanism: a reduction over a huge dimension to few outputs: every block reduces a chunk, a second pass combines the partials

realizations.how: Grid of a few blocks per SM, each reduces a contiguous chunk to one partial; a second tiny kernel (or the last block, via an atomic counter) reduces the partials.

techniques.mechanism: mean and variance in one pass with Welford's update (merge partials with Chan's formula): one read of the input instead of two
risks: the naive one-pass E[x^2]-E[x]^2 loses precision; Welford does not

realizations.how: Per thread: Welford (count, mean, M2) over its elements; combine across lanes / warps with Chan's merge; then normalise in the same kernel with the row still on chip.
Vector Welford over strip-mined chunks, merge the lane partials at the end.

techniques.mechanism: max and normaliser in one pass with running rescaling (m, l), then one write pass: two reads of the row become one
risks: rescale the running sum when the max changes: l = l * exp(m_old - m_new) + exp(x - m_new)

realizations.how: One block (or warp) per row: each thread keeps (m, l) over its elements, combine across lanes with the rescaling merge, then write exp(x - m) / l in a second sweep over registers / on-chip memory.
Strip-mined pass computing running max and rescaled sum (vfredmax + polynomial exp), then the write pass.

techniques.mechanism: pooling windows overlap: stage the input tile plus halo once and let each thread compute several outputs from it

realizations.how: One thread per output (or a strip of outputs along W) reading a staged input tile; for non-overlapping windows (stride == kernel) just vectorise the loads along W.

techniques.mechanism: global / adaptive pooling and mean over H x W: one block (or warp) per (n, c) plane with a tree reduction

realizations.how: Grid over N*C planes; threads stride over the H*W elements with vectorised loads; warp / block reduction; one store per plane.

techniques.mechanism: per-row top-k with a small register / on-chip heap or bitonic network instead of a full sort

realizations.how: One warp per row: each lane keeps its k best in registers (k small), then a warp-level bitonic merge; radix select for large k.
